name: Wavelength
description: Point-of-care ultrasound education for emergency and acute clinicians: consultant-led hands-on courses, free Wavelength Pearls and Wavelength Academy e-learning. Mapped to the RCEM curriculum, taught by FAMUS-accredited instructors and RCEM-approved ultrasound supervisors.

director.name: Dr Firas Abou-Auda
director.title: Consultant in Emergency Medicine
bio: Firas is a Consultant in Emergency Medicine and the Ultrasound Lead at Darent Valley Hospital in Kent. He has scanned in emergency care for {scanYears} years, since 2008, and has run ultrasound courses for {teachYears} years, since 2010. He is a FAMUS instructor and supervises clinicians through the FAMUS accreditation pathway.

He sits on the EUSEM Ultrasound Committee and the Emergency Ultrasound Curriculum Task Force, and he examines for and writes content for the European Board Examination in Emergency Medicine. He is an ALS and ATLS instructor.

team.name: Dr Zahra Habibzadeh
team.title: Emergency Medicine Specialist
bio: Zahra is an emergency medicine specialist and an experienced ultrasonographer, with years of hands-on scanning in acute and emergency care.
As General Manager she runs Wavelength day to day, from course planning and venues to bookings and delegate support, and brings a sonographer's eye for image quality to every course.

learnTopics._help: Topic groups for the Pearls and Academy pages, in display order. Each pearl and module joins the topic whose categories list its category. A category not listed here shows under "More pearls". Add a topic by copying one object and giving it a new slug. Topics with a "page" also get their own landing page at /learn/<page>/ (heading, seoTitle and about paragraphs) once they hold three or more live pearls.

topics.label: Fundamentals
topics.intro: Set up the machine and the image before you look for pathology.

topics.label: Heart and vessels
topics.intro: Cardiac views, the venous system, the aorta and the leg veins.
topics.heading: Cardiac and vascular ultrasound
topics.seoTitle: Cardiac and vascular POCUS: echo, IVC, aorta and DVT
about: Focused cardiac ultrasound answers a few questions in a breathless or shocked patient: is the left ventricle squeezing, is the right ventricle under strain, is there fluid around the heart, and how full is the venous system? These pearls take each question in turn, with the view, the measurement and the trap that catches new scanners.
The vascular pearls cover compression ultrasound for proximal DVT, the Baker's cyst which mimics it, and the femoral pseudoaneurysm after a puncture. Each one ends with a short test.

topics.label: Lung and airway
topics.intro: Pneumothorax, consolidation, effusion, the diaphragm and tube position.
topics.heading: Lung ultrasound and the airway
topics.seoTitle: Lung ultrasound: pneumothorax, effusion and consolidation
about: Lung ultrasound beats the supine chest X-ray for pneumothorax, pleural effusion and consolidation, and it needs only a few views. These pearls start with the pleural line and lung sliding, then move to fluid above the diaphragm, air bronchograms, diaphragm movement and confirming tube position after intubation.
Each pearl teaches one sign, the pitfall which makes it misleading, and a short test to check what stuck.

topics.label: Abdomen and pelvis
topics.intro: Free fluid, the gallbladder and bile duct, kidneys, bladder, stomach, bowel and the pelvis, in adults and children.
topics.heading: Abdominal and pelvic ultrasound
topics.seoTitle: Abdominal and pelvic POCUS: eFAST, biliary, renal and pelvis
about: Point-of-care ultrasound of the abdomen and pelvis answers focused questions at the bedside: is there free fluid, is the bile duct dilated, is the kidney obstructed, is the bladder full, is the bowel obstructed, and is there an intrauterine pregnancy?

These pearls cover eFAST, the gallbladder and common bile duct, hydronephrosis and pyonephrosis, the bladder, the stomach, small bowel obstruction, appendicitis, intussusception in children, and pelvic pain in women, including ectopic pregnancy and ovarian torsion.

topics.label: Soft tissue and joints
topics.intro: Collections, foreign bodies, tendons and joint effusions.
topics.heading: Soft tissue and musculoskeletal ultrasound
topics.seoTitle: MSK and soft tissue ultrasound: abscess, tendon and joint
about: Soft tissue and musculoskeletal ultrasound settles common emergency department questions in minutes: abscess or cellulitis, a retained foreign body, a torn tendon, fluid in a joint, or a dislocated shoulder before and after reduction.

These pearls cover abscess and necrotising fasciitis, foreign bodies, hernias, Achilles, quadriceps and distal biceps tears, tendon anisotropy, and effusions of the hip, knee and shoulder, each with a short test.

topics.label: Nerve blocks
topics.intro: Ultrasound-guided regional anaesthesia for pain in the emergency department.
topics.heading: Ultrasound-guided nerve blocks
topics.seoTitle: Ultrasound-guided nerve blocks for emergency analgesia
about: Ultrasound-guided regional anaesthesia gives targeted pain relief for fractures, wounds and dislocations, with less need for opioids and procedural sedation. These pearls describe the anatomy, the probe position and the target for each block used in emergency care.

They cover the femoral nerve, infra-inguinal and supra-inguinal fascia iliaca and PENG blocks for hip fractures, serratus anterior plane and erector spinae plane blocks for rib fractures, rectus sheath, greater occipital, superior trunk and SHAC blocks, and the median, ulnar, radial and digital nerve blocks for the hand. Follow your local guidance on training, monitoring and local anaesthetic doses.
